column1: # tools/oracle/css_style_diff.py: how a key of the computed-style differential is classified when css_style_divergences.txt is written (--write-list).
# Columns, tab separated: a regular expression that matches a whole key, the class, the reason. The first rule that matches wins. The list the gate reads is
# css_style_divergences.txt; these rules only save writing it again for a population of other seeds (a hunt), and a key that no rule matches is

column3: CSS Inline 3 (served 2026-10-26) gives alignment-baseline the values "baseline | <baseline-metric>" and the initial value baseline, with no `auto`; for an empty attribute (dropped, so the initial value stands) Chromium still writes the `auto` of SVG 1.1, Firefox and this library `baseline`

two causes, Chromium alone in both: its user agent style sheet gives an SVG `text` element `display: block` where the initial value of display is `inline` (the sheet is each engine's own; SVG 2 leaves it to the user agent); and it computes `display: contents` to `none` on an `a` and on a `textPath`, where Display 3, Appendix B says "display: contents strips the element from the formatting tree, and hoists its contents up to display in its place." for a container that is rendered, "any valid content inside a tspan or textPath" being hoisted (Firefox and this library hoist both; both browsers compute a `switch` to none, and so does this library)
the initial value of font-family is "depends on user agent" in the pin, so no answer is wrong; Chromium writes the name of its default family and Firefox and this library the generic `serif`

Values 4 (served 2026-10-26), Appendix C: "When CSS is being parsed in quirks mode, <quirky-length> is a type of <length> that is only valid in certain properties"; Chromium takes a number as a length in the style attribute of an SVG element in a document that is in standards mode, as SVG 1.1 did, and Firefox and this library do not

SVG 2 Styling (served 2026-10-26): "Since presentation attributes are parsed as CSS values, not declarations," the CSS-wide keywords are values of the attribute as of any property; Chromium reads these geometry attributes as SVG lengths and writes 0px, Firefox and this library the keyword's value

SVG 2 Styling (served 2026-10-26): a presentation attribute is "parsed as a value of that property", and `5.` is no CSS <number>, so the attribute is dropped and the initial value `auto` stands; Chromium reads it with the SVG number syntax and writes 0px
SVG 2 Geometry (served 2026-10-26): "A negative value for rx is invalid and must be ignored." (and the same for ry and r); Chromium keeps the negative length, Firefox and this library drop it

SVG 2 Coordinate Systems (served 2026-10-26): "User agents must support the transform property and presentation attribute as defined in css-transforms-1."; Chromium writes `none` for the attribute, Firefox and this library the matrix

SVG 2 Painting (served 2026-10-26) gives the keywords "auto | optimizeSpeed | crispEdges | geometricPrecision" and "auto | sRGB | linearRGB" with their capitals, and a computed value "as specified"; both engines write the keyword in lower case, this library as the grammar spells it

SVG 2 Paths (served 2026-10-26) gives the property d the grammar `none | <string>` and says "The contents of the <string> value must match the svg-path EBNF grammar defined below"; the engines implement the CSS Shapes `path()` function, which that text does not have, and write a path of the attribute in their own normal form (Chromium upper case commands, Firefox keeps the case), `none` for a string that is no path data; this library keeps the string as written and does not read the path data (that is the renderer's)

Fonts 4 (served 2026-10-26): "The user agent may fine-tune these values for different fonts or different types of display devices." The absolute-size keywords are a table of guidelines (large is 6/5 of medium, 19.2px, which this library writes), and both engines use 18px; a length in em computed from it follows; the digits of a computed length are not specified either (the engines write six significant digits, this library six decimals)

CSSOM resolved values: "then the resolved value is the used value."; the engines answer the used length of a number or percentage line-height and this library its computed value (the number, or the length of the percentage of the font size, which the engines take from their own font size table)

CSSOM resolved values: "then the resolved value is the used value."; an SVG element without a CSS layout box has the used transform origin 0 0, and the engines write that where this library writes the computed value 50% 50% 0px
Fill and Stroke 3 (served 2026-10-26): "Values less than 1 are invalid (and make the declaration invalid)."; the engines keep 0.5 where this library drops it

SVG 2 Coordinate Systems (served 2026-10-26): "User agents must support the transform property and presentation attribute as defined in css-transforms-1.", whose syntax is the CSS one; both engines read the attribute with the SVG 1.1 syntax only and write `none`

SVG 2 Coordinate Systems (served 2026-10-26): "User agents must support the transform property and presentation attribute as defined in css-transforms-1."; the attribute is the property, so its value is the list of functions (`rotate(45deg)`); Chromium writes `none` and Firefox the matrix of the list
